title: Hardcoding System Traversal through Temporal Decomposition
pattern: Breaking a system into separate classes/modules where each step represents a chronological step of execution (temporal order) and duplicates structural knowledge of file/protocol structures.
why_bad: It causes information leakage. If the format of the file/protocol changes, all three independent chronological classes must be modified, increasing change amplification and risk of divergence.
detection: Separate structs or modules whose names match a chronological verb chain (e.g. `Loader`, `Modifier`, `Writer`) that all pass raw representations of the same format data.
counterexample:
Encapsulating format structure in a cohesive engine while using action verbs for pure processing steps:
```rust
struct Engine;
```
source: *A Philosophy of Software Design* by John K. Ousterhout (Chapter 5.3, p. 23).
